summary: RESOURCE LEDGER (C++). (1) Adoption marker <data_dir>/echo.db.adopting: owner adopt_legacy_echo_db (one boot-time caller, agents/core/src/agent.cpp:885, before any plugin init); acquired by yuzu::shared::write_file_atomic (exclusive-create temp file guarded by TempFileGuard, fd owned by FdOwner, fsync file and parent on POSIX, rename; no flush-by-handle on Windows) before the first sidecar rename; released by fs::remove after the main-file rename, or at the next boot when tar.db is gone; transfer none; failure cleanup: a failed write returns before anything moves, a failed removal warns and is retried at the next boot. (2) Marker read handle: function-local std::ifstream in a block scope, 256-byte capped read, closed before the marker is rewritten or removed (an open handle blocks ReplaceFileW and remove on Windows); early returns cannot leak it. (3) Login-database state: function-local UtmpSession (Linux) and UtmpxSession (macOS), constructor setutent/setutxent, destructor endutent/endutxent, copy deleted, ends the session on every exit including a throwing push_back. (4) /proc/<pid>/cmdline read: bounded std::string (kProcReadCap 256 KiB), noexcept, istream owned by the caller. (5) HourlySeenSet batch journal: std::vector<std::string> admitted_ and bool batch_open_, members of tcp_closing_seen_ and module_seen_, mutated only under collect_mu_; cleared by commit_batch and rollback_batch; bound is the keys admitted per tick, not the set cap (an overflow or hour clear does not clear the journal); begin_batch rolls back an open batch; NOT RAII (see W4-S3). (6) GatewayRouteStore::set_legacy_echo_wire_name: one pooled connection via try_acquire_for(kWriteTimeout 500 ms) under RAII lease, PgResult RAII, session-guarded UPDATE, fail-open at the call site. No new thread, subprocess, callback context, socket, FILE*, sqlite3 handle or allocated C string. The in-repo docs/resource-ledgers/echo-db-budget.md must carry these rows and must drop the stale COPY wording (W4-B5).
